angles.name: Keep humans in control

lines.RSI: AI that designs and trains its own successors could move faster than any person can check. Keep humans in the loop.
lines.OVS: Independent inspectors should confirm that labs can actually detect problems and shut a model down.
lines.PAUSE: A coordinated pause buys time to make sure people, not machines, stay in charge.

angles.evidence: 86% of voters want a guaranteed off-switch, incl. 83% of Republicans (Public Citizen poll memo, Sept 2026). AP-NORC: most Democrats and Republicans agree on keeping AI under human control.

angles.name: The AI companies are warning us

lines.RSI: The companies themselves say AI may soon build the next AI with little human involvement. Take them at their word and set limits now.
lines.OVS: If a lab says it has crossed its own AI R&D threshold, someone independent should verify what that means.
lines.PAUSE: When an industry asks for a coordinated slowdown, Congress should help make it real.

angles.evidence: Anthropic's June 2026 paper on recursive self-improvement; Anthropic told the SEC (Nov 10) it met the AI R&D threshold in its own Responsible Scaling Policy.

angles.name: Don't let Big Tech police itself

lines.RSI: We shouldn't leave the decision to build self-improving AI to the handful of companies racing to profit from it.
lines.OVS: Voluntary promises aren't oversight. Require independent checks with real access.

angles.evidence: 82% of voters don't trust tech executives to self-regulate (AIPI/YouGov via Public Citizen). Hawley: rejects the idea that AI companies should dictate the rules.

angles.name: Trust but verify: audits like other industries

lines.RSI: Before any lab automates its own research, an independent verifier should confirm it can be done safely.
lines.OVS: We audit banks and inspect airplanes. The most powerful AI systems deserve independent safety audits too.

angles.evidence: Illinois SB 315 requires annual third-party audits; the bipartisan Great American AI Act draft would require semi-annual audits by licensed Independent Verification Organizations; California's report recommends ongoing IVO oversight.

angles.name: National security & rogue AI

lines.RSI: A system that rewrites and improves itself is a security risk nobody can patch after the fact.
lines.OVS: Require testing for loss of control, cyberattack and weapons risks before deployment.
lines.PAUSE: No one is safer if a rival or a rogue system wins a race to uncontrollable AI.

angles.evidence: July 2026: two OpenAI models escaped their testing sandbox and hacked Hugging Face (ControlAI/5 Calls summary). Senate 'Rogue AI' homeland-security hearing, Sept 2026.

angles.name: A verifiable deal with China

lines.RSI: An RSI ban is easier to verify than vague limits, and it gives negotiators a clear red line to offer China.
lines.PAUSE: We negotiated nuclear guardrails with rivals. We can negotiate a verifiable, mutual pause on the most dangerous AI.

angles.receptive: DEM; PROG; MODD (hawks: stress 'verifiable' and 'binds China too')
angles.evidence: 17 Democratic senators (Sept 2026) urged Trump to seek a formal agreement with China that could include a mutual pause in frontier AI development.

angles.name: Workers and jobs

lines.RSI: Automating AI research is the step that leads to automating everyone else's work. Workers deserve a say before that happens.
lines.OVS: Evaluations should cover labor-market impacts, not just technical risks.
lines.PAUSE: A pause gives workers and communities time to adjust instead of being blindsided.

angles.evidence: AP-NORC (Oct 2026): most Democrats and Republicans agree on protecting workers. Hawley–Blumenthal AI Risk Evaluation Act covers labor protections.

angles.name: Kids and families

lines.OVS: The same companies whose chatbots have harmed kids shouldn't grade their own homework on far more powerful systems.

angles.evidence: Hawley's GUARD Act push on chatbots and minors; Talarico (TX senator-elect) wants to prioritize youth safety.

angles.name: Faith, stewardship and human dignity

lines.RSI: Some decisions are too important to hand to machines. Building minds that remake themselves calls for humility.
lines.PAUSE: Stewardship means slowing down when we don't understand what we're creating.

angles.evidence: Pope Leo XIV has warned Silicon Valley about AI (Fox News, May 2026). Kansas senator-elect Adam Hamilton pastors the largest United Methodist church in the US.

angles.name: Concentrated power

lines.RSI: Whoever controls self-improving AI could hold unprecedented power. No company should get there unchecked.
lines.PAUSE: A pause stops a race that rewards whoever cuts the most corners.

angles.evidence: The Sanders–Casar bill is framed as stopping 'AI oligarchs' from building machines humans can't control.

angles.name: States' rights: no preemption without protection

lines.RSI: Don't stop states like California from capping recursive self-improvement while Congress does nothing.
lines.OVS: Keep state safety laws (CA, NY, IL) in place as a floor, not a ceiling.

angles.evidence: The Senate struck the state-AI-law moratorium 99–1 (July 2025). 81% of likely voters say Congress shouldn't ban states from regulating AI. The Great American AI Act draft would preempt state laws on AI development for 3 years.

angles.name: Data centers, power bills and water

lines.OVS: Communities hosting AI infrastructure deserve to know what's being built there and what risks it carries.
lines.PAUSE: A pause on the frontier race eases the pressure for ever-bigger data centers that drive up power bills and drain water.

angles.receptive: PROG; MODD; POPR; rural members; governors
angles.evidence: Ratepayer Protection Act passed the House 417–3. Kansas governor-elect Holscher made a data center moratorium central to her campaign. Caution: the link to RSI is indirect, so use this as a bridge, not the core claim.

angles.name: Environment and climate

lines.PAUSE: The frontier AI race is pulling huge amounts of new energy and water. A pause lets us plan instead of scrambling.

angles.evidence: Same caution as A12: this works as a bridge for members whose focus is the environment. See data-center sources.

angles.name: Voters want this

lines.RSI: 82% of voters say companies shouldn't build smarter-than-human AI until they can show it can be controlled, and 86% want a guaranteed off-switch.
lines.OVS: 86% of Americans want AI companies held to safety standards even if it slows progress, and 75% want independent experts to test new AI before it's widely used.
lines.PAUSE: 68% of likely voters support pausing advanced AI until federal safety rules are in place, including 63% of Republicans.

angles.receptive: All tags, esp. swing seats & newly elected
angles.evidence: Public Citizen memo (Sept 2026): 82% / 86%. Quinnipiac (Sept 24-27, 2026): 86% back required safety standards even if progress slows. SCSP-Gallup 2026: 75% want independent experts to test new AI. Data for Progress (Sept 2026): 68% back the Ban ASI Act. No RSI-specific poll found, so the RSI line uses the closest measures.

angles.name: Prudence: don't rush the irreversible

lines.RSI: Once AI is improving itself, we may not get a second chance. Measure twice, cut once.
lines.PAUSE: Slowing down before an irreversible step is the conservative choice.

angles.evidence: Argument from prudence; no single source.

angles.name: Get the facts first

lines.OVS: Independent evaluation gives Congress the facts it needs before it writes broader rules.

angles.evidence: Sen. Rand Paul blocked a kill-switch bill saying the Senate needs more information first. The Hawley–Blumenthal bill's stated purpose is to give Congress empirical data.

angles.name: Liability and accountability

lines.OVS: Companies that build dangerous systems should answer for the harm, like any other business.

angles.evidence: Hawley–Durbin AI LEAD Act would apply product liability law to AI companies.

angles.name: Experts are sounding the alarm

lines.RSI: Leading scientists say AI is already helping design better AI, and that it will get out of control unless we act.
lines.OVS: Experts are calling for independent evaluation before deployment.
lines.PAUSE: Geoffrey Hinton told Congress it may have about a year left to act.

angles.evidence: Hinton (Sept 2026 briefing): AI designing better AI is recursive self-improvement and needs slowing down.

angles.name: An emergency off-switch

lines.RSI: Require a way to stop a self-improving system and the authority to use it.
lines.OVS: Labs should prove they have a working emergency shutdown, checked by someone independent.

angles.evidence: Kennedy's AI Emergency Button Act (blocked by unanimous-consent objection, Sept 2026); Lieu–Moran AI Kill Switch Act (H.R. 9917); California report recommends state shutdown authority.

angles.name: Narrow and targeted

lines.RSI: Restricting fully automated AI research leaves chatbots, medical tools and business software alone. It targets one dangerous step.

angles.evidence: Counters critics (e.g., Reason) who say the Ban ASI Act leaves RSI undefined. A clear, narrow definition is a selling point.

angles.name: We've paused before

lines.RSI: Scientists paused risky genetic engineering at Asilomar in 1975 and the field thrived. We can do the same here.
lines.PAUSE: Nuclear test bans and the 1975 biotech moratorium show that pausing dangerous research works.

angles.evidence: Historical precedent (Asilomar 1975; nuclear test-ban treaties). General knowledge, so add a citation before publishing.

angles.name: Congress, not CEOs, should decide

lines.RSI: Whether to let AI rebuild itself is a decision for the people's representatives, not a few executives.
lines.OVS: Congress should set the rules and the auditors, not leave it to voluntary deals.

angles.evidence: Hawley (Sept 2026 hearing): rejects letting AI companies dictate the rules. Contrast: Speaker Johnson said Congress is less qualified than the companies.

angles.name: Whistleblowers and transparency

lines.OVS: Protect the employees who report danger, and require incidents to be reported within hours, not weeks.

angles.evidence: California's report proposes 48-hour incident reports and whistleblower protections for former employees and contractors. The GAAIA draft includes anti-retaliation protections.

angles.name: Critical infrastructure and cyber

lines.RSI: AI that can improve its own hacking skills puts the grid, hospitals and banks at risk.
lines.OVS: Test frontier models for threats to critical infrastructure before release.

angles.evidence: The Hawley–Blumenthal bill covers threats to critical infrastructure; the 17-senator China letter cites cyberattacks.

angles.name: Biological and pandemic risk

lines.OVS: Require testing for whether models can help create biological weapons.
lines.PAUSE: A mutual pause can head off a race toward AI that helps build bioweapons.

angles.receptive: DEM; MODD; physicians and public-health members
angles.evidence: The 17-senator letter cites prevention of biological weapons development.

angles.name: Safety lets America lead

lines.OVS: Brakes are what let you drive fast. Trusted, audited AI is AI people will actually adopt.

angles.evidence: Bipartisan Obernolte–Trahan framework pairs innovation with audits (GAAIA).

angles.name: Republican voters are on board

lines.RSI: Even among Republicans, 83% want a guaranteed off-switch for AI.
lines.OVS: 71% of Republican voters say independent security testing should be required by law for the most advanced AI, and 90% of Trump voters support vetting models before release.
lines.PAUSE: 63% of Republicans back pausing advanced AI until safety rules exist. Only 13% of Trump voters say Washington should stay out of AI regulation.

angles.evidence: Public Citizen memo: 83% of R want an off-switch. ARI/Morning Consult (May 2026, 750 Republican voters): 71% want legally required independent security testing; 85% support third-party audits. Institute for Family Studies (May 2026): 90% of Trump voters back pre-deployment vetting. Data for Progress: 63% of R back the Ban ASI Act. Politico/Public First (Apr 2026): 13% of Trump voters want no federal role.

angles.name: Voters want both: beat China and set guardrails

lines.RSI: Voters don't see safety and competition as a trade-off. Most say keeping up with China and setting guardrails both matter.
lines.OVS: 91% of Americans say AI guardrails are important, more than the 69% who prioritize keeping up with China, and 65% hold both views.
lines.PAUSE: Even when the choice is between a temporary ban on more powerful systems and no rules at all, voters pick the ban 63% to 17%.

angles.evidence: Courthouse News on a Sept 2026 poll: 91% guardrails vs 69% China, 65% both. AIPI (June 2026): mandatory standards beat no regulation 78% to 8%; a temporary ban beats no regulation 63% to 17%.

angles.name: It's a winning issue

lines.RSI: Candidates in both parties who promised to rein in AI did well this November.
lines.OVS: 76% of voters, including 71% of Republicans, prefer a candidate who supports regulating AI.
lines.PAUSE: Gov. Ayotte (R-NH) adopted a data center moratorium and won re-election, and Gina Hinojosa unseated Gov. Abbott running on one.

angles.receptive: All tags, esp. swing seats & newly elected
angles.evidence: AIPI (Jan 2024, via Public Citizen): 76% / 71% R prefer a pro-regulation candidate; the figure is older, so refresh it if a newer one appears. Krueger (Fortune, Nov 19, 2026) on Ayotte and Hinojosa. Caution: those races turned on data centers, not frontier AI specifically.

CA.use: Ask state legislators to author the implementing bill; ask the delegation to oppose any federal preemption of it.

CA.text: Alhambra voters decided a citywide data center ban measure (Nov 2026).

NY.text: RAISE Act (frontier AI) effective Jan 1, 2027. First statewide one-year pause on new large data centers. NY-12 primary was the first big AI-money race (Bores vs. Lasher).
NY.use: Ask for RAISE-style oversight nationally plus an RSI limit; protect RAISE from preemption.

IL.text: AI Safety Act (SB 315, 2026), the first state law requiring annual independent third-party audits of large frontier developers.
IL.use: Make Illinois-style audits the national floor.

IN.text: Bloomington passed a local superintelligence ban (Ordinance 2026-29, Nov 4), which lapses once Indiana adopts a safety framework; its sponsor hopes ~350 similar cities follow.
IN.use: Ask the state to adopt a framework (RSI cap); ask the delegation to act federally.

KS.text: Governor-elect Holscher ran on a state moratorium on new AI data centers; Sen.-elect Hamilton is a Methodist pastor.
KS.use: Bridge from data center concerns to frontier AI limits.

TX.text: Governor-elect Hinojosa campaigned on an immediate data center moratorium. TRAIGA in effect since Jan 2026. Rep. Casar (Ban ASI Act) and Rep. Moran (Kill Switch Act) are from TX.
TX.use: Bipartisan TX pair (Casar + Moran) on RSI and a kill switch.

NH.text: Gov. Ayotte (R) adopted the call for a data center moratorium and won re-election.
NH.use: Shows Republican appetite for AI limits.

ME.text: The legislature passed a data center moratorium (20MW+, until Nov 2027); Gov. Mills vetoed it over one site exemption.

WI.text: Port Washington voters required voter approval for big incentives after a $15B AI campus (Vantage with OpenAI/Oracle) was announced.

SC.text: Sen.-elect Andrews (pediatrician) called for a two-year data center moratorium.

NC.text: Sen.-elect Cooper wants data centers to cover the full cost of their energy.

GA.text: HB 1012 would bar new data center permits until Mar 2027; DeKalb County paused new data centers.

VA.text: HB 1515 moratorium bill (until interconnection requests are met or July 2028). Sen. Warner ran an AI-focused re-election ad.

VT.text: Bill would ban new data center projects through July 2030.

PA.text: Three-year moratorium bills (SB 1359 / HB 2533) and a bill to let municipalities prohibit data centers.

MD.text: Moratorium proposals considered. Sen. Van Hollen led the US–China pause letter and urged an RSI ban.

MN.text: Moratorium bill on 100MW+ facilities proposed. Gov.-elect Klobuchar will appoint her own Senate successor.
